hero.headline: Pick the country. We'll handle everything that isn't studying.
hero.subhead: Kimere is a young consultancy built entirely around the part of moving abroad nobody warns you about — applications, visas, funding, documents, somewhere real to live. We work towards any destination you choose, and we go deepest in Italy, where we run the whole route ourselves, on the ground.
hero.ctaInstitution: I'm a university or an agency

routing.heading: Four very different problems. Take the one that's yours.
routing.body: A student who knows where they're going, a student who doesn't, a university opening a new corridor and an agency adding a destination need almost nothing in common from us. So we don't pretend otherwise — pick your situation and skip everything else.

boxes.title: I want to study abroad
boxes.body: You've more or less chosen. What's left is the application, a visa file that survives your consulate, funding you probably don't know you qualify for, and a lease that turns out to be real.

boxes.title: I don't know what to choose
boxes.body: Course, country, or whether to leave at all. You fill in a questionnaire, we research your actual options before we speak, and you finish the session with a plan instead of forty tabs open.

boxes.title: I work for a university
boxes.body: You want students from abroad, but the destination's funding and recognition rules are a black box — and so is what your candidates can actually afford. The first online seminar is free and built on your market.

boxes.title: I run a recruitment agency
boxes.body: You recruit; we become your operation on the ground. The boundary between us and the commission split are written down before the first student moves, not renegotiated after.

strengths.heading: We speak your language. Not as a slogan.
strengths.body: Leaving your country is frightening in a way no brochure admits, and what helps most is obvious the first time you see it work: talking to someone from where you're from, in the language you actually think in. That's how this team is built — independent professionals spread across several countries, coordinated by one person who answers to you.

points.title: Someone from your country, where we cover it
points.body: Where our team covers where you're from, that's who takes your call. The cultural shorthand you don't have to explain saves entire conversations — and it's the reason universities abroad agree to the meeting in the first place.

points.title: A network, not a head office
points.body: Specialists in several countries rather than one building with a phone queue. There's usually someone awake in your timezone, and nobody gets passed between departments because there are no departments.

points.title: Seven languages, and they're in-house
points.body: The teachers who run our language courses are the same people who handle document translation. That isn't a quirk of the org chart — it's why a translation can start the day you ask instead of going out to a supplier.

bureaucracy.eyebrow: The part that actually stops people
bureaucracy.heading: Almost nobody fails the admission. They fail the paperwork.
bureaucracy.body: Getting in is rarely where it goes wrong. It goes wrong on a funding application you never heard of, closing on a date nobody mentioned, and a diploma that isn't legally usable abroad in the form you're holding. In Italy — the market where we go deepest — that's three specific fights.

items.title: Scholarships and the ISEE
items.body: Italy's right-to-study funding is means-tested, and your eligibility runs through the ISEE — an income indicator almost no family abroad has heard of, let alone knows how to calculate. We work it out and file on its own deadline, which is not your university's deadline and does not wait for it.

items.title: Translating and legalising your diploma
items.body: Your qualification has to arrive in Italian and legally valid, and that sequence is where months quietly disappear. Our own translators do the translation and we run the legalisation file alongside you, instead of leaving you in a queue behind someone else's outsourcing.

items.title: Fees, health cover, a bank account
items.body: Tuition brackets that move with your declared income, health cover you can't enrol in without a fiscal code, and an account you need before you can pay for any of it. Boring, strictly sequential, and the usual place an academic year gets lost.

bureaucracy.limitHeading: What we can't do — better you hear it here
bureaucracy.limitBody: The comparability statement for a foreign qualification is issued by CIMEA or assessed by the university itself, and nothing we do replaces it or makes it optional. What we do is build the file, follow it through, and keep the translation in-house so that step isn't the one holding you up. Anyone telling you the requirement can be skipped is selling you a rejected application.

forUniversities.heading: Push your university past its own borders
forUniversities.body: Universities lose international candidates to a rulebook neither side can read. A student in Buenos Aires might qualify for Italian public tuition scaled to family income, plus a maintenance grant on top — and if nobody at either end knows that, they enrol somewhere more expensive instead. Closing that gap is the entire conversation.
forUniversities.seminarHeading: It starts with a free seminar
forUniversities.seminarBody: We get on a call with your team and build the session around your market rather than ours. Where your students want to go, what that country actually funds, what its paperwork will demand of them — answered for your case, with the published sources attached.
seminarPoints: Built on the destination you care about, whether that's Italy or not
Funding, fees and qualification recognition answered from published sources
No cost and no commitment on the first session
A written summary your office keeps, whatever you decide afterwards

languageCourses.heading: Learn the language before you need it
languageCourses.body: The team that handles your documents also teaches the languages, so the two never end up as separate companies you have to introduce to each other. Courses run with freelance teachers who are native or fluent in what they teach, online, around a student's timetable rather than an office's.

finalCta.heading: None of the four felt like yours?
finalCta.body: Then start with a strategic consultation. It's one session, and it ends with a plan rather than a brochure — because the research happens before we meet, not while you watch.
finalCta.surveyNote: It begins with a questionnaire, and that's the point: it's what lets us research your actual case in advance instead of spending your session asking basic questions.
